title: A Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized-withdrawal study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of expanded dosing regimens for Xywav in adult participants with narcolepsy or idiopathic hypersomnia
official: A Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized-withdrawal study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of expanded dosing regimens for Xywav in adult participants with narcolepsy or idiopathic hypersomnia
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the efficacy of expanded dosing regimens of Xywav in participants with narcolepsy and participants with idiopathic hypersomnia (IH) on excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Is 18 to 75 years of age (inclusive) at the time of signing the informed consent.
2. If currently prescribed non-oxybate anticataplectic medications for cataplexy (NT1 only), must agree to taper off these medications (under the guidance and instruction of the investigator) during the OL-TOP and remain off these medications through the end of the DBRWP. Note that an exception will be made for participants who are prescribed these medications for other indications (exclusion criterion 12).
3. If currently treated with nicotine replacement therapy, has been taking the same dosage for at least 1 month prior to screening and has no current plans to adjust the dosage during the study period.
4. A female participant is eligible to participate if she is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and one of the following conditions applies: − Is a WONCBP as defined in Protocol Appendix 4 Contraceptive and Barrier Guidance OR − Is a WOCBP and using a contraceptive method that is highly effective (with a failure rate of < 1% per year), preferably with low user dependency as described in Appendix 4 Contraceptive and Barrier Guidance, during the study intervention period and for at least 7 days after the last dose of study intervention and agrees not to donate eggs (ova, oocytes) for the purpose of reproduction during this period. The investigator should evaluate the potential for contraceptive method failure (eg, noncompliance, recently initiated) in relationship to the first dose of study intervention. • A WOCBP must have a negative highly sensitive (serum) pregnancy test result as required by local regulations during screening • Additional requirements for pregnancy testing during and after study intervention are provided in the protocol • The investigator is responsible for review of medical history, contraception history, menstrual history, and recent sexual activity to decrease the risk of inclusion of a woman with an undetected early pregnancy.
5. Is capable of giving signed informed consent, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and in this protocol.
6. Is willing and possesses the ability to comply with the study design schedule and other study requirements (eg, completing assessments as specified, complying with study dosing instructions).
7. Has a primary diagnosis of IH meeting ICSD-3 criteria or narcolepsy (NT1 or NT2) meeting ICSD-3 or DSM-5 criteria.
8. Participants with a primary diagnosis of NT1 must have a history of at least 14 cataplexy attacks in a typical 2-week period, based on participant history at the time of diagnosis and prior to initiating treatment.
9. Participants with a primary diagnosis of IH must have an average total nightly sleep time of at least 7 hours, based on participant history at the time of diagnosis and prior to initiating treatment.
10. If not currently treated with oxybate, has clinically significant symptoms of EDS with an ESS score > 11 at screening and baseline.
11. If currently treated with oxybate, must have documented improvement of EDS with oxybate treatment per the investigator’s clinical judgement.
12. If currently treated with oxybate, has been taking the same stable dosing regimen at a total nightly dosage of 3 g to 9 g (inclusive) for at least 2 months at screening.
13. If previously treated with (and not currently taking) oxybate, must have been off oxybate treatment for at least 2 weeks prior to screening. Must not have previously discontinued oxybate due to reasons related to intolerability, safety, or lack of efficacy.
14. If currently treated with alerting agents, has been taking the same dosage for at least 1 month prior to screening and has no current plans to adjust the dosage during the study period. Note: Alerting agents refer to either traditional stimulants (eg, amphetamines, methylphenidates) or wake-promoting agents (eg, modafinil, pitolisant, solriamfetol). (Note that OX2R agonists are not permitted during the study [exclusion criterion 13]).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Shows evidence of a previous untreated or inadequately treated sleep disorder considered by the investigator to negatively impact the conduct of the study, including  sleep-disordered breathing (Apnea Index > 10, using the US CMS rules [CMS.gov]),  parasomnias, circadian rhythm sleep disorders, or restless legs syndrome determined by a previous sleep-laboratory diagnosis or interview utilizing modules of the Diagnostic  Interview for Sleep Patterns and Disorders.
2. Has any severe drug allergy or a history of allergic or severe adverse reactions (asthma, urticaria) or intolerance to Xyrem, Xywav, GHB, or any components of the dosage forms.
3. Has a history of substance abuse based on DSM-5 criteria and/or a positive urine drug screen for drugs of abuse or alcohol (with the exception of a positive urine drug screen for a permitted concomitant medication).
4. Has recently taken (ie, within 1 month prior to screening), is taking, or plans to take any of the following: a. A substance or medication contraindicated with Xywav use, specifically alcohol and sedative hypnotics (ie, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, non-benzodiazepine hypnotics) b. A medication with a known drug-drug interaction with Xywav (ie, valproic acid or divalproex sodium) c. Medications known to have clinically significant CNS sedating effects: − Dual orexin receptor antagonists (ie, suvorexant, lemborexant, daridorexant) − Melatonin receptor agonists (ie, ramelteon, tasimelteon) − Antipsychotics − Antiepileptics or antidepressants with known substantial sedation profiles (except when used as an anticataplectic agent). Note that participants who are prescribed non-oxybate anticataplectic medications for cataplexy (NT1 only) will taper off these medications (under the guidance and instruction of the investigator) during the OL-TOP and remain off these medications through the end of the DBRWP (inclusion criterion 10). An exception will be made for participants who are prescribed these medications for other indications (eg, depression), provided they have been taking the same stable dosage for at least 6 months and have no current plans to adjust the dosage during the study period. − Opioid analgesics − General anesthetics d. Other medications, natural health products, or substances from which the participant experiences clinically significant sedation (eg, sedating antihistamines or natural sleep aids). For the duration of the study, participants must abstain from these medications/substances. Treatment must have been discontinued for at least 2 weeks or 5 half-lives prior to enrollment (whichever is longer). The investigator may use clinical judgement in allowing the continuation of medications that are not otherwise excluded and that may have CNS sedating effects, provided that the participant has been on a stable dose (ie, at least 1 month with no current plans to adjust the dose). Note: This list of prohibited medications is not   exhaustive. A more comprehensive list of prohibited medications is provided in the investigator site file.
5. Has recently taken (ie, within 1 month prior to screening), is taking, or plans to take an OX2R agonist during the study.
6. Has tobacco-use disorder or uses vaping products that impact sleep (ie, a participant who routinely wakes during the night to smoke or vape).
7. Has excessive caffeine consumption that may impact sleep (ie, participant routinely consumes > 4 caffeinated beverages per day [400 mg/day caffeine]).
8. Has received any other investigational drug within 30 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to screening or plans to use an investigational drug (other than the study intervention) during the study.
9. Has a laboratory value(s) at screening outside the laboratory reference range (eg, ALT or AST > 3 × ULN) or ECG abnormalities considered to be clinically significant that could affect the safety of the participant or interfere with study efficacy or safety assessments or with the ability of the participant to complete the study per the judgement of the investigator. Note: Screening laboratory tests and ECG may be repeated once to assess eligibility.
10. Was previously eligible for this study but discontinued study intervention or was withdrawn early.
11. Has an occupation that requires nighttime or variable shift work.
12. Has succinic semi-aldehyde dehydrogenase deficiency by medical history.
13. Has plans for travel across more than 3 time zones during the study.
14. Has uncontrolled hypothyroidism as determined by central clinical laboratory test results.
15. Has a current seizure disorder.
16. Has a history of head trauma associated with loss of consciousness in the past 5 years or if an event occurred more than 5 years prior to screening, experiences sequelae due to the event.
17. Has a history or presence of bipolar disorder, bipolar-related disorders, schizophrenia, schizophrenia spectrum disorders, or other psychotic disorders according to DSM-5 criteria.
18. Has a history or presence of any unstable or clinically significant medical condition (eg, chronic pain condition that may impact sleep), behavioral or psychiatric disorder (including active suicidal ideation as measured by a positive response to items 4 or 5 on the Baseline/Screening C-SSRS, or current or past [within 1 year] major depressive episode), or history or presence of another neurologic disorder or surgical history that might affect the participant’s safety and/or interfere with the conduct of the study, in the opinion of the investigator.
19. Has any other significant disease or disorder that, in the opinion of the investigator, may either put the participant, other participants, or study staff at risk because of participation in the study, may influence the result of the study, or may affect the participant’s safety or ability to take part in the study.
20. Any past or current medical conditions or experience that, in the investigator’s clinical judgment, would preclude treatment with a once-nightly dose > 6 g up to 7.5 g dose or twice-nightly regimen with a total nightly dosage > 9 g up to 12 g (divided into 2 doses).
